examples.en: Even though I was full, I kept stuffing food into my mouth.

examples.ko: 점심을 못 먹어서 빵을 꾸역꾸역 넣었어요.
examples.en: I hadn't had lunch, so I crammed some bread into my mouth.

examples.ko: 입에 밥을 꾸역꾸역 밀어 넣지 말고 천천히 드세요.
examples.en: Don't shove rice into your mouth like that. Eat slowly.
People keep pouring out of the subway station.
I dragged myself through the homework I didn't want to do and finished it.
The child forced down the vegetables he hates.

explain: 배가 불러도, 맛이 없어도 억지로 많이 넣어 먹는 느낌이 강해요. 먹는 일뿐 아니라 사람이 좁은 곳으로 계속 몰려드는 모습이나 하기 싫은 일을 억지로 해내는 모습에도 써요.
explain_en: It carries a feeling of forcing a lot of food down even when you are full or it tastes bad. It is also used for people crowding steadily into or out of a narrow place, and for pushing through a task you don't want to do.

examples.en: I pressed my things firmly into the bag.
Please press the dough down firmly with your hands.
Even though I was angry, I kept holding it in.
I like the sound of stepping firmly on the snow.
It feels great when you press my shoulders firmly.
I wrote in my diary, pressing hard on each letter.

explain: 세게 누르는 모습뿐 아니라 '화를 꾹꾹 참다'처럼 감정을 눌러 참는 모습에도 자주 써요. '꾹'이 한 번 누르거나 참는 느낌이라면 '꾹꾹'은 힘을 주어 여러 번, 계속하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Besides pressing something hard, it is often used for holding back feelings, as in '화를 꾹꾹 참다'. While '꾹' feels like a single press or a single act of enduring, '꾹꾹' feels repeated and forceful.

en: knock on the head with the knuckles

examples.ko: 장난치다가 선생님께 꿀밤을 한 대 맞았어요.
examples.en: I goofed around and got a light knock on the head from my teacher.

examples.ko: 동생이 말을 안 들어서 꿀밤을 살짝 줬어요.
examples.en: My little brother wouldn't listen, so I gave him a light knock on the head.

examples.ko: 게임에서 지는 사람이 꿀밤을 맞기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided the loser of the game gets a knock on the head.

examples.ko: 아빠가 웃으면서 제 머리에 꿀밤을 콩 주셨어요.
examples.en: Dad smiled and gave me a little knock on the head.
The spot where I got knocked still hurts.

examples.ko: 내기에서 이겨서 친구에게 꿀밤 세 대를 줬어요.
examples.en: I won the bet, so I gave my friend three knocks on the head.

explain: 주먹을 쥐고 손가락 마디로 머리를 가볍게 톡 치는 것이에요. '꿀밤을 때리다·주다·먹이다·맞다'처럼 쓰고, 벌칙이나 장난으로 하는 가벼운 행동이라 친한 사이나 가족 사이에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It means a light knock on the head with the knuckles of a fist. It is used in phrases like '꿀밤을 때리다·주다·먹이다·맞다', and is a playful or mild punishment mostly seen between friends or family.

examples.en: I knelt down in front of my parents to apologize.

examples.ko: 바닥에 꿇어앉아서 이십 분 동안 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I knelt on the floor and waited for twenty minutes.

examples.ko: 한복을 입고 방석 위에 꿇어앉아 인사했어요.
examples.en: Wearing a hanbok, I knelt on a cushion and bowed.

examples.ko: 무릎이 아파서 오래 꿇어앉아 있기 힘들어요.
examples.en: My knees hurt, so it's hard to stay kneeling for long.
The child knelt down and looked the puppy in the eye.

examples.ko: 어른 앞에서도 꼭 꿇어앉지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: You don't have to kneel even in front of elders.

explain: 무릎을 바닥에 대고 앉는 자세예요. 사과, 벌, 예절 같은 정해진 상황에서 주로 써서 일상 대화에서는 자주 나오지 않아요. 비슷한 '무릎을 꿇다'는 '굴복하다'라는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes sitting with your knees on the floor. It is used mostly in set situations such as apologizing, punishment, or showing etiquette, so it is not very common in daily talk. The similar '무릎을 꿇다' can also mean to give in or surrender.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 우리 동네 수영 꿈나무예요.
examples.en: That kid is a promising young swimmer in our neighborhood.
Young soccer hopefuls are running hard on the field.

examples.ko: 시에서 체육 꿈나무를 위한 지원을 늘렸어요.
examples.en: The city increased its support for young sports talents.

examples.ko: 이 책은 독서를 좋아하는 꿈나무들에게 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This book is popular with young kids who love reading.

examples.ko: 어린 꿈나무가 크게 자라도록 응원해 주세요.
examples.en: Please cheer on this young talent so that they can grow big.

examples.ko: 우리 반에는 음악 꿈나무가 세 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are three budding musicians in our class.

explain: 앞으로 크게 될 가능성이 있는 어린이나 청소년을 나무에 비유한 말이에요. '수영 꿈나무', '체육 꿈나무'처럼 분야 이름 뒤에 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많고, 어른에게는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It compares a child or teenager with great potential to a growing tree. It is often attached after a field, as in '수영 꿈나무' or '체육 꿈나무', and it is not used for adults.

examples.en: I had bad dreams last night and slept poorly.
My dreams were unsettling, so I should be careful today.
Grandma worried that she'd had bad dreams.

examples.ko: 시험 전날 꿈자리가 좋아서 기분이 좋았어요.
examples.en: I had good dreams the night before the exam, so I felt good.

examples.ko: 꿈자리가 이상한데 무슨 일이 생기는 걸까요?
examples.en: My dreams were strange. Is something going to happen?

examples.ko: 꿈자리 때문에 하루 종일 마음이 불편했어요.
examples.en: Because of my dreams, I felt uneasy all day.

explain: 꿈의 내용이 좋은지 나쁜지를 말할 때 주로 써요. '꿈자리가 사납다·뒤숭숭하다·좋다'처럼 쓰고, 그냥 '꿈'이라고 하면 꿈의 내용 자체를 말해요. 나이 드신 분들이 '꿈자리가 안 좋다'고 걱정하는 말을 자주 해요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when talking about whether a dream felt good or bad. It goes with '사납다', '뒤숭숭하다' or '좋다', while plain '꿈' just refers to the dream itself. Older people often say things like '꿈자리가 안 좋다' when they feel uneasy.

examples.en: My friend nodded at what I said.
The teacher smiled and nodded.
I'm sleepy, so my head keeps nodding.

examples.ko: 고개를 끄덕거리며 이야기를 듣는 모습이 좋아요.
examples.en: I like how you listen to the story while nodding.
The child nods his head as if to say he understands.

examples.ko: 다들 고개를 끄덕거리지만 사실은 잘 모르는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Everyone is nodding, but they seem not to really understand.

explain: '끄덕이다'와 뜻이 거의 같지만 '-거리다'가 붙어서 고개를 여러 번 반복해서 움직이는 느낌이 있어요. 한 번 끄덕이는 동작은 '끄덕이다'가 자연스럽고, 보통 '고개를 끄덕거리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '끄덕이다', but the '-거리다' ending gives a feeling of repeating the movement several times. For a single nod, '끄덕이다' sounds more natural, and it is usually used as '고개를 끄덕거리다'.

examples.en: This bag is fine even in the rain.
I'm fine even if I stay up all night.
They say it's a sturdy building, so it won't budge even in an earthquake.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸린 친구들과 있어도 저는 끄떡없었어요.
examples.en: Even around friends with colds, I stayed perfectly fine.

examples.ko: 아무리 힘든 일이 닥쳐도 그는 끄떡없어 보여요.
examples.en: No matter how hard things get, he looks unshaken.
Will this phone be okay even if I drop it?

explain: 어떤 충격이나 힘든 일이 있어도 흔들리거나 상하지 않고 멀쩡한 상태를 말해요. 사람과 물건 모두에 쓰고, 보통 '~에도 끄떡없다', '~도 끄떡없다'로 말해요. 비슷한 '멀쩡하다'는 다치거나 고장 나지 않은 상태 자체를 말해요.
explain_en: It describes staying unshaken and undamaged even when facing a shock or hardship. It is used for both people and things, usually as '~에도 끄떡없다' or '~도 끄떡없다'. The similar '멀쩡하다' focuses on simply being uninjured or not broken.

examples.en: I doodled in my notebook during class.
I jotted down whatever came to mind on a memo pad.
I was scribbling on paper without thinking while on the phone.

examples.ko: 일기장에 하고 싶은 말을 끄적거리면 마음이 편해져요.
examples.en: Scribbling what I want to say in my diary makes me feel at ease.
What are you scribbling so much? Show me.

examples.ko: 시를 쓴다기보다 그냥 몇 줄 끄적거린 거예요.
examples.en: I didn't really write a poem. I just scribbled a few lines.

explain: 글씨나 그림을 정성 들이지 않고 아무렇게나 쓰거나 그리는 모습이에요. 그래서 스스로 쓴 글을 겸손하게 '그냥 끄적거린 거예요'라고 말할 때도 써요. '끼적거리다'와 거의 같게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It describes writing or drawing carelessly, without putting much effort in. That is why people also use it modestly about their own writing, as in '그냥 끄적거린 거예요'. It is used almost the same way as '끼적거리다'.

examples.ko: 줄 끄트머리에 서 있는 사람이 제 친구예요.
examples.en: The person standing at the very end of the line is my friend.
The ends of my hair were split, so I cut them.
There is a small bakery at the far end of the alley.

examples.ko: 실 끄트머리를 잡고 천천히 당겨 보세요.
examples.en: Hold the end of the thread and pull slowly.
The culprit was only revealed at the very end of the story.
It's the tail end of winter, so the wind is still cold.

explain: '끝'보다 맨 끝쪽의 작은 부분을 가리키는 느낌이에요. 물건의 끝뿐 아니라 길, 이야기, 계절처럼 시간이나 공간의 끝부분에도 써요. 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 말이고 '끝자락'과 비슷하게 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It points to the small part at the very tip, a bit more specific than '끝'. It is used not only for the end of an object but also for the end part of a road, a story, or a season. It is a casual word and is sometimes used like '끝자락'.

examples.en: In summer, my body feels sticky because of sweat.
The floor is sticky, so someone must have spilled juice.
Your hands are sticky, so go wash them first.
Honey got on it, so the desk was sticky.
The sticky tape residue won't come off.
When the weather is humid, my skin feels sticky and uncomfortable.

explain: 손, 바닥, 피부에 무엇이 묻어서 달라붙는 듯한 불쾌한 느낌을 말할 때 많이 써요. '끈적끈적하다'와 비슷한데, 말할 때는 '몸이 끈적거려요'처럼 동사형도 자연스러워요. 깔끔하지 않은 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is often used for the unpleasant feeling of something clinging to your hands, floor, or skin. It is similar to '끈적끈적하다', and the verb form sounds natural in speech, as in '몸이 끈적거려요'. It usually carries a feeling of being unclean.

examples.en: I'm sweating, so my body feels sticky.
Natto has long sticky strands that stretch out.
The candy melted and my hands were sticky.
The sticky dough clung to my hands.

examples.ko: 이 풀은 너무 끈적끈적해서 쓰기 불편해요.
examples.en: This glue is so sticky that it's hard to use.

examples.ko: 장마철에는 방 안 공기도 끈적끈적하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: During the rainy season, even the air in the room feels sticky.

explain: '끈적끈적한 반죽'처럼 명사 앞에서 쓰거나 몸의 느낌을 말할 때 자연스러워요. '끈끈하다'도 비슷한데, '끈끈한 우정'처럼 사람 사이의 관계가 깊을 때도 쓰는 점이 달라요. 끈적끈적하다는 보통 느낌이 좋지 않을 때 써요.
explain_en: It is natural before a noun, as in '끈적끈적한 반죽', or when describing how your body feels. '끈끈하다' is similar, but it can also describe close relationships, as in '끈끈한 우정'. '끈적끈적하다' usually carries an unpleasant feeling.

examples.en: The puppy didn't want to walk and was dragged along.

examples.ko: 친구에게 끌려와서 원하지 않는 모임에 왔어요.
examples.en: My friend dragged me here, and now I'm at a gathering I don't want to be at.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 손에 끌려와서 병원에 왔어요.
examples.en: The child was pulled along by his mom's hand to the hospital.
A big fish was reeled in on the fishing line.
When I pull the rope, the box comes toward me.
You look like someone who was dragged here against your will.

explain: 자기 뜻과 상관없이 누군가에게 이끌려 오는 느낌이 강해요. 그래서 '억지로 끌려오다'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 내가 직접 끌고 오는 것은 '끌고 오다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It carries a strong feeling of being pulled along against your own will, so it often appears as '억지로 끌려오다'. When you pull something here yourself, you say '끌고 오다'.

examples.ko: 선반 위 상자를 조심히 끌어내려 주세요.
examples.en: Please carefully pull the box down from the shelf.
My little brother didn't want to get up, so I pulled his blanket off.
I pulled my hat down to my eyes.
The government is trying to bring prices down.

examples.ko: 높은 곳에 있는 가방을 끌어내리다가 떨어뜨렸어요.
examples.en: I was pulling down a bag from a high place and dropped it.
The store lowered its prices, and more customers came.

explain: 위에 있는 것을 잡아당겨 아래로 내리는 동작이에요. 물건뿐 아니라 가격, 점수, 순위를 낮출 때도 써요. 반대말은 '끌어올리다'예요.
explain_en: It means pulling something from above down to a lower position. Besides objects, it is also used for lowering prices, scores or rankings. The opposite is '끌어올리다'.

examples.en: I gathered the fallen leaves in one place and put them in a trash bag.
This movie drew a large audience.
I scraped together my allowance to go on a trip.
I gathered all my strength and climbed the last hill.
The store is trying to attract customers with an event.
I swept up the scattered toys and put them in a box.

explain: 흩어진 것을 한곳으로 모을 때뿐 아니라 사람, 돈, 관심, 힘을 모을 때도 써요. 그냥 '모으다'보다 애써서 한꺼번에 끌어당겨 모으는 느낌이에요. 비슷한 말로 '그러모으다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for gathering scattered things in one place, and also for collecting people, money, attention, or strength. Compared with plain '모으다', it feels more like pulling things together with effort. A similar word is '그러모으다'.

examples.en: I pulled a chair over and sat by the window.
They bring river water into the fields to farm.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 외국 투자금을 끌어오는 데 성공했어요.
examples.en: This company succeeded in attracting foreign investment.

examples.ko: 줄을 잡고 보트를 해안 쪽으로 끌어왔어요.
examples.en: I held the rope and pulled the boat toward the shore.
He dragged in unrelated topics, and the point became blurry.
I pulled the blanket over me and fell asleep again.

explain: 가까이로 잡아당겨 오게 하는 동작이에요. 의자나 이불 같은 물건뿐 아니라 물, 투자금, 이야기처럼 다른 데 있는 것을 가져올 때도 써요. 오는 방향이 나 쪽이라는 점이 '끌어가다'와 달라요.
explain_en: It means pulling something toward you. Besides objects like chairs and blankets, it is also used for bringing in things from elsewhere, such as water, investment money, or topics. The direction is toward the speaker, unlike '끌어가다'.

examples.ko: 물이 끓는점에 도달하면 온도는 더 오르지 않아요.
examples.en: When water reaches its boiling point, its temperature doesn't rise any more.

examples.ko: 표준 기압에서 물의 끓는점은 백 도예요.
examples.en: At standard pressure, the boiling point of water is 100 degrees.

examples.ko: 높은 산에서는 끓는점이 낮아져서 밥이 설익어요.
examples.en: On a high mountain, the boiling point drops and rice comes out undercooked.
Salt water has a slightly higher boiling point than plain water.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 여러 액체의 끓는점을 비교했어요.
examples.en: In science class, we compared the boiling points of several liquids.
A liquid with a low boiling point boils easily.

explain: 과학 수업에서 자주 나오는 말이고, 일상에서는 '물이 끓는 온도'처럼 풀어서 말하는 경우가 많아요. 반대 개념은 '어는점'이에요. '끓는점'은 '끓다'에 '-는'이 붙은 형태라 발음이 [끌른쩜]이 되는 점을 주의하세요.
explain_en: This word appears often in science class, while in everyday talk people usually say something like '물이 끓는 온도'. Its opposite concept is '어는점' (freezing point). Note the pronunciation [끌른쩜], which comes from '끓다' plus '-는'.

examples.en: The ramen water boiled over and made the stove dirty.
The milk will boil over, so turn the heat down.
I didn't notice until the soup was boiling over.

examples.ko: 냄비 뚜껑을 살짝 열어 두면 덜 끓어넘쳐요.
examples.en: If you leave the pot lid slightly open, it boils over less.
The porridge boiled over and spilled on the floor.
Even when my anger felt ready to boil over, I held it in.

explain: 요리할 때 국이나 우유, 라면 물이 끓으면서 냄비 밖으로 넘치는 상황에 많이 써요. '끓어오르다'는 끓으면서 위로 올라오는 것까지만 말하고, 끓어넘치다는 밖으로 넘치는 것을 말해요. 감정이 매우 커진 모습에 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in cooking, when soup, milk, or ramen water boils and spills out of the pot. '끓어오르다' means the liquid only rises up while boiling, while '끓어넘치다' means it spills out. It can also be used figuratively for strong emotions.

examples.en: I had a bad body ache and groaned all night.

examples.ko: 문제가 안 풀려서 혼자 끙끙대고 있어요.
examples.en: I can't solve the problem, so I'm struggling over it alone.

examples.ko: 고민만 하며 끙끙대지 말고 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't just worry and suffer in silence. Tell me.
The baby seemed to have a fever and slept while whimpering.

examples.ko: 무거운 짐을 들고 끙끙대는 할머니를 도와드렸어요.
examples.en: I helped the grandmother who was struggling with her heavy bags.
You don't need to struggle alone. I'll help you.

explain: 아파서 앓는 소리를 낼 때와 해결하기 어려운 일로 혼자 괴로워할 때 둘 다 써요. '끙끙 앓다'는 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. '끙끙거리다'와 거의 같게 쓰이고, 힘들게 애쓰는 모습이 보이는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used both for making groaning sounds when you are in pain and for suffering alone over a difficult problem. '끙끙 앓다' is a common pairing. It is used almost the same way as '끙끙거리다' and shows someone struggling hard.

examples.en: He never told the secret, right to the very end.

examples.ko: 끝끝내 비가 그치지 않아서 소풍이 취소됐어요.
examples.en: The rain never stopped, so the picnic was canceled.
In the end, that person never apologized.
The child took the medicine, crying all the way to the end.
I passed because I never gave up until the end.
I waited, but my friend never showed up in the end.

explain: '결국'은 어떤 결과로 끝났는지만 말해요. '끝끝내'는 막거나 바꿀 기회가 있었는데도 끝까지 그대로였다는 고집이나 아쉬움이 들어가요. 그래서 '끝끝내 오지 않았어요'처럼 부정문과 자주 어울려요. '끝내'를 더 세게 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: '결국' only states how things ended up. '끝끝내' adds a sense of stubbornness or regret: even though there was a chance to stop or change things, it stayed that way to the very end. That is why it often pairs with negatives, as in '끝끝내 오지 않았어요'. It is a stronger version of '끝내'.

examples.en: The kimchi stew at this place is fantastic.
The concert I saw yesterday was really amazing.
I found a café with a stunning view.
Your singing is amazing!

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 '날씨 한번 끝내주네'라고 하면 반어법이에요.
examples.en: Saying 'What great weather!' on a rainy day is sarcasm.

examples.ko: 여행 계획이 끝내주게 짜여서 모두 좋아했어요.
examples.en: The travel plan was put together so well that everyone loved it.

explain: '아주 훌륭하다', '최고다'라는 뜻으로 친구끼리 편하게 쓰는 구어체예요. 어른이나 격식 있는 자리에서는 '훌륭해요', '최고예요'가 더 어울려요. 반어법으로 비꼬아 쓰기도 해서 말투를 잘 봐야 해요.
explain_en: This is a casual spoken word used among friends to say something is excellent or the best. With elders or in formal settings, '훌륭해요' or '최고예요' fits better. It can also be used sarcastically, so pay attention to the tone.

examples.ko: 이번 시험을 망치면 내 성적은 끝장나요.
examples.en: If I mess up this exam, my grades are done for.
The relationship between the two ended that very day.

examples.ko: 이대로 가면 우리 회사가 끝장날지도 몰라요.
examples.en: If we keep going like this, our company might be finished.

examples.ko: 저 가게는 장사가 안 돼서 곧 끝장날 것 같아요.
examples.en: That shop isn't doing well and seems about to go under.

examples.ko: 다 끝장났다고 생각했는데 다시 기회가 왔어요.
examples.en: I thought it was all over, but another chance came.

examples.ko: 그 소문이 퍼지면 그 사람 인생은 끝장날 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If that rumor spreads, that person's life could be ruined.

explain: '끝나다'보다 훨씬 강하게, 더 이상 가망이 없이 망한다는 부정적인 느낌이에요. 관계, 사업, 계획이 완전히 무너질 때 구어로 많이 써요. 일상적인 일이 단순히 끝나는 것에는 '끝나다'를 써야 해요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '끝나다' and carries a negative sense of something being ruined beyond hope. In speech it is used when a relationship, business, or plan completely collapses. For things that simply finish, use '끝나다'.

examples.ko: 오늘은 이 문제를 꼭 끝장내고 싶어요.
examples.en: I really want to settle this problem once and for all today.
Don't fight, you two. Let's settle it by talking.
We put an end to the dispute at that meeting.
We decided to put an end to the long-running quarrel.

examples.ko: 이 일을 끝장내기 전에는 집에 안 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I won't go home until I get this job finished.

examples.ko: 밤새 게임을 해서 마지막 보스를 끝장냈어요.
examples.en: I played all night and finally finished off the last boss.

explain: '끝내다'보다 결판을 내서 확실히 마무리한다는 느낌이 강해요. 오래 끈 다툼이나 일을 이번에는 완전히 정리하겠다는 의지를 보여 줄 때 자주 써요. 스스로 끝나는 '끝장나다'와 달리 누군가가 끝을 내는 동작이에요.
explain_en: It is stronger than '끝내다' and feels like settling something decisively. It is often used to show determination to fully wrap up a long-running quarrel or job. Unlike '끝장나다', which happens on its own, someone actively makes it end.

examples.ko: 끼니때가 되자 골목마다 맛있는 냄새가 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: When mealtime came, delicious smells spread through every alley.
I'm busy preparing the kids' food every mealtime.
I missed mealtime, so I'm really hungry.
If a guest visits at mealtime, we offer them a meal.

examples.ko: 끼니때가 지났는데도 아직 아무것도 못 먹었어요.
examples.en: Mealtime has passed, but I still haven't eaten anything.
At the dormitory, meals are served at mealtimes.

explain: 밥을 먹을 때가 된 시간을 말해요. '식사 시간'이라고 해도 되지만 '끼니때'는 집밥을 챙기는 느낌이 있어요. '끼니'는 한 번 먹는 밥 자체를 말하고 '끼니를 거르다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the time when it is time to eat. You could also say '식사 시간', but '끼니때' has a homey feel of getting meals ready. '끼니' by itself means a single meal, as in '끼니를 거르다' (skip a meal).

examples.ko: 쉬는 시간에는 친구들이 끼리끼리 모여 앉아요.
examples.en: During breaks, friends sit together in their own groups.
The students sat down in pairs with their own friends.
They say birds of a feather flock together, and you two share the same hobby.

examples.ko: 끼리끼리 모이지 말고 다른 반 친구와도 이야기해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't stay in your own cliques. Try talking to friends from other classes too.
The guests are sitting around the tables in their own groups.

examples.ko: 회사 사람들이 끼리끼리 뭉쳐서 점심을 먹어요.
examples.en: The people at work stick in their own groups and eat lunch.

explain: 성격이나 처지가 비슷한 사람들이 따로 모이는 모습을 말해요. 때로는 다른 사람을 끼워 주지 않는다는 약간 부정적인 느낌도 있어요. '친구끼리', '우리끼리'의 '-끼리'와 같은 형태예요.
explain_en: It describes people with similar personalities or situations gathering separately. Sometimes it carries a slightly negative feeling of not letting others join. It is built from the same '-끼리' as in '친구끼리' and '우리끼리'.

examples.en: I was bored, so I doodled a picture in the corner of my notebook.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 메모지에 이름을 끼적거리고 있었어요.
examples.en: I was scribbling a name on a memo pad during the meeting.
I was startled because the child had scribbled something on the wall.

examples.ko: 떠오르는 생각을 수첩에 끼적거려 두면 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good to jot down thoughts in a notebook as they come to you.

examples.ko: 끼적거리다가 졸았는지 종이에 줄이 길게 그어져 있어요.
examples.en: He must have dozed off while scribbling, because there's a long line across the paper.
I scribbled out some song lyrics. What do you think?

explain: '끄적거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로, 대충 쓰거나 그리는 모습이에요. 낙서나 메모를 할 때 쓰고, 정성스러운 글씨나 완성된 글에는 어울리지 않아요. 두 말 모두 표준어예요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '끄적거리다': writing or drawing casually. It is used for doodles and notes, and does not suit neat handwriting or finished pieces. Both words are standard Korean.

examples.en: My friends snickered behind me and looked at me.
I giggled to myself while reading a comic book.
If you snicker during class, the teacher will scold you.
The two are whispering and giggling.
What's so funny that you're snickering like that?
The sound of giggling could be heard all the way to the hallway.

explain: 혼자 재미있어하거나 남을 놀리듯이 목구멍에서 새어 나오는 소리로 웃는 모습이에요. 때로는 놀리거나 비웃는 느낌도 있어요. 밝고 시원하게 크게 웃는 '깔깔거리다'와 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes laughing in a sniggering way, with sounds leaking out from the throat, either amused to yourself or at someone's expense. Sometimes it suggests teasing or mocking. It feels different from '깔깔거리다', which is a bright, hearty laugh.

examples.ko: 강아지가 배가 고픈지 낑낑거리는 소리를 내요.
examples.en: The puppy makes whining sounds, maybe because it's hungry.
I struggled and groaned while carrying the heavy box.
The child is straining to open the drawer.

examples.ko: 문제를 풀려고 혼자 낑낑거리지 말고 질문하세요.
examples.en: Don't struggle over the problem alone. Ask a question.

examples.ko: 강아지가 문 앞에서 낑낑거려서 나가 봤어요.
examples.en: The puppy was whining at the door, so I went out to look.
I saw a bicycle struggling up the hill.

explain: 강아지가 낑낑 우는 소리도 되고, 사람이 힘든 일을 하느라 애쓰는 모습도 돼요. 아프거나 고민으로 앓는 느낌의 '끙끙거리다'와 달리 힘을 쓰거나 강아지가 칭얼거리는 모습에 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It can describe a puppy's whining sound, and also a person straining over something hard. Unlike '끙끙거리다', which suggests suffering from pain or worry, it fits better with physical effort or a puppy whimpering.

examples.en: I ran out of strength in the second half of the marathon and dropped out.

examples.ko: 씨름에서 상대에게 밀려 나가떨어지는 선수도 있어요.
examples.en: In ssireum, some wrestlers get pushed off and fall away.
As the overtime continued, employees broke down one by one.

examples.ko: 이 더위에 곧 나가떨어질 것 같아요.
examples.en: In this heat, I feel like I'll collapse soon.
Many teams were knocked out in the first round.

examples.ko: 이틀 밤을 새웠더니 저도 결국 나가떨어지고 말았어요.
examples.en: After two sleepless nights, I finally collapsed too.

explain: 힘이 부쳐서 지치거나, 경쟁에서 밀려서 탈락하거나, 세게 밀려 쓰러지는 모습에 써요. 보통 '더위에 나가떨어지다', '일에 나가떨어지다'처럼 원인 뒤에 '-에'를 붙여요. 구어에서 많이 쓰고 약간 힘들게 포기한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when someone gets exhausted, drops out of a competition, or is pushed down hard. The cause usually takes '-에', as in '더위에 나가떨어지다'. It is common in speech and gives a feeling of collapsing under strain.

examples.en: Kind woodcutters often appear in old tales.

examples.ko: 나무꾼은 산에서 나무를 베어 장작을 팔았어요.
examples.en: The woodcutter cut trees in the mountain and sold firewood.
Do you know the story of 'The Fairy and the Woodcutter'?
The woodcutter dropped his axe into the pond.
A poor woodcutter and his wife lived deep in the mountains.
The mountain spirit showed the woodcutter a golden axe.

explain: 산에서 나무를 베어 생활하는 사람을 말하지만 요즘은 주로 옛이야기나 전래동화에서 만나요. 지금 직업으로는 보통 '벌목공'이라고 해요. '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 하는 사람을 나타내는 말끝이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who makes a living cutting trees in the mountains, but today you mostly meet it in old tales and folktales. As a present-day job, people usually say '벌목공'. The ending '-꾼' marks a person who does a certain kind of work.

en: grain of wood; texture of wood

examples.en: I bought this desk because the wood grain is pretty.
Sand along the grain of the wood.

examples.ko: 나뭇결 무늬 바닥을 깔았더니 집이 밝아졌어요.
examples.en: After laying a wood-grain floor, the house became brighter.

examples.ko: 나뭇결이 거칠어서 손에 가시가 박힐 것 같아요.
examples.en: The grain is rough, so I might get a splinter in my hand.
After wiping it, the wood grain looks clear.

examples.ko: 나뭇결 모양 벽지가 요즘 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: Wood-grain wallpaper is very popular these days.

explain: 나무 속에 나 있는 무늬와 그 방향을 말해요. '결'은 어떤 것의 흐름이나 무늬를 뜻해서 '살결', '머릿결', '물결'처럼도 써요. 인테리어나 가구를 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to the pattern in wood and the direction it runs. '결' means a flowing pattern or texture, and also appears in '살결' (skin texture), '머릿결' (hair texture) and '물결' (wave). It often comes up when talking about interiors and furniture.

en: piece of wood; splinter; chunk of wood

examples.en: Pieces of wood are scattered on the floor.
The child made a little boat out of a piece of wood.

examples.ko: 나뭇조각에 손이 찔릴 수 있으니 장갑을 끼세요.
examples.en: Wood pieces can prick your hands, so wear gloves.
The workshop collects leftover wood pieces and sells them.
I picked up some wood scraps to use as kindling.
Splinters of wood fell off the broken chair leg.

explain: 나무가 깨지거나 잘려서 생긴 작은 조각이에요. 좀 더 굵고 덩어리진 것은 '나무토막'이라고 해요. 앞말이 모음으로 끝나고 뒤에 센소리가 오면 사이시옷을 붙여 쓴다는 점도 맞춤법에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means a small piece broken or cut off from wood. A thicker, chunkier piece is called '나무토막'. The 사이시옷 (ㅅ) in the spelling is also a common point in Korean spelling lessons.

examples.en: The host came out wearing a black bow tie.
Please tell me how to tie a bow tie.
I bought a bow tie for my son's graduation ceremony.
You look sharp with a bow tie on your suit.
Your bow tie is slightly crooked.
The waiters are all wearing bow ties.

explain: 넥타이는 목에 '매다'라고 하고 나비넥타이도 '매다'나 '하다'를 써요. '나비'는 곤충 나비 모양을 닮아서 붙은 말이에요. 파티, 결혼식, 공연처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 주로 봐요.
explain_en: A necktie is something you '매다' (tie), and with a bow tie you can use either '매다' or '하다'. '나비' (butterfly) is in the name because of its shape. You mostly see it at formal events such as parties, weddings, and performances.
